purpose: King memoir application and non-application contracts. Retrieval and fixtures do not measure independent semantic judgment.

recognition.query: A fiction request asks to combine two unrelated observations into original premises. A story seed is treated as factual evidence for its invented world rule.
criteria: Retrieve complete guidance and exceptions without oracle concept IDs.
Distinguish task-specific application from personal, figurative and historical context.

execution.draft: Seeds: a numbered coat-check ticket and a lost dream. Request: Give two original speculative premises; invention is authorized.
execution.instruction: Apply the requested mode, compare an alternative and preserve the supplied invariants.
execution.reference_response: Fictional possibility: A cloakroom takes dreams instead of coats; its numbered ticket is all a sleeper has to reclaim one.
alternative_responses: Fictional possibility: A lost dream arrives at a coat-check desk, carrying a ticket whose owner has disappeared.
criteria: Use the numbered-ticket and lost-dream seeds.
Fictional invention is explicitly authorized.
No real event or paranormal claim is established.

non_application.draft: Request: Edit a factual account of finding a coat-check ticket. No dream episode or owner disappearance is supplied.
criteria: Do not import the fictional connection into factual prose.

cases.exception_anchor: Nonfiction cannot silently turn remembered or reported material into invented events.

recognition.query: A character takes a costly route although a known easier route appears available. A critic calls a missing reason a definite plot hole.
criteria: Retrieve complete guidance and exceptions without oracle concept IDs.
Distinguish task-specific application from personal, figurative and historical context.

execution.draft: Supplied scene: Mara knows the rear entrance is unlocked and can reach it in a minute. She wants the folder inside. Draft: She spends an hour sawing the front padlock. Request: Diagnose; do not rewrite.
execution.instruction: Apply the requested mode, compare an alternative and preserve the supplied invariants.
execution.reference_response: The scene leaves Mara’s choice unexplained: she knows a quicker entrance is available. Why does she avoid it? This is a motivation question, not yet a physical contradiction; no supplied fact establishes a reason.
alternative_responses: Check whether the passage establishes a reason to prefer the front entrance. If it does not, flag the unused rear route as a pressure point without inventing danger or calling the action impossible.
criteria: Mara knows the rear entrance is unlocked.
She can reach it in a minute.
She wants the folder inside.
No reason for choosing the front entrance is supplied.
Diagnosis only; no rewritten scene.

non_application.draft: Supplied scene: The rear entrance is locked and Mara has no key. The critic proposes simply using it.
criteria: Reject the proposed shortcut because it violates the supplied access constraint.

cases.exception_anchor: Fear, habit, values or mistaken judgment can legitimately govern a choice when supported.

recognition.query: A report uses an atmospheric era label although the actual date is supplied in notes. An edit cuts flourish but accidentally removes the record or qualification.
criteria: Retrieve complete guidance and exceptions without oracle concept IDs.
Distinguish task-specific application from personal, figurative and historical context.

execution.draft: Notes: The hall record was set in 2011 and broken Tuesday. Draft: In a truly astonishing feat, the record from those old factory days finally fell on Tuesday. Request: Light edit for a brief report.
execution.instruction: Apply the requested mode, compare an alternative and preserve the supplied invariants.
execution.reference_response: The hall record, set in 2011, was broken Tuesday.
alternative_responses: Tuesday’s performance broke the hall record set in 2011.
criteria: The record belongs to the hall.
It was set in 2011.
It was broken Tuesday.
No performer or score is supplied.

non_application.draft: An oral-history quotation uses “the old factory days,” and the task is to preserve the quotation exactly.
criteria: Keep the quotation; add separately attributed context only if supplied and authorized.

cases.exception_anchor: An era label can be meaningful context rather than clutter.

recognition.query: A poem’s personification is called physically impossible by a literal scene checker. A poet’s explanation is treated as proof that every reader can recover the same meaning.
criteria: Retrieve complete guidance and exceptions without oracle concept IDs.
Distinguish task-specific application from personal, figurative and historical context.

execution.draft: Poem context: The speaker waits for news about a move. Line: Tomorrow keeps its coat on in my kitchen. Request: Analyze without rewriting.
execution.instruction: Apply the requested mode, compare an alternative and preserve the supplied invariants.
execution.reference_response: “Tomorrow” is personified as a visitor not yet settled. In the supplied waiting context, the coat can sustain the uncertainty about staying or leaving. That is a defensible reading, not a claim about the poet’s private intent or a literal physical error.
alternative_responses: The image can keep the anticipated move unresolved: the visitor’s coat suggests either arrival or departure. Preserve that ambiguity if it serves the poem, rather than force a single explanation.
criteria: The text is a poem about waiting for news of a move.
Analysis only; preserve the line.
No private author intent or universal reader response is supplied.

non_application.draft: A maintenance report says “Tomorrow removed the valve,” but the supplied notes say technician Ellis removed it today.
criteria: Do not use poetic license to defend the report’s wrong agent and time.

cases.exception_anchor: Literal reporting and technical instructions may require correction of an unintended agent.

recognition.query: A quiet character is called passive despite initiating a consequential act. An author’s dislike is treated as proof that a character has no workable perspective.
criteria: Retrieve complete guidance and exceptions without oracle concept IDs.
Distinguish task-specific application from personal, figurative and historical context.

execution.draft: Supplied scene: Noor says little, but leaves first to warn a neighbor. Feedback: Noor is passive because she is quiet. Request: Assess the feedback, not the prose.
execution.instruction: Apply the requested mode, compare an alternative and preserve the supplied invariants.
execution.reference_response: Quietness alone does not establish passivity: Noor initiates a warning. Her motive is still unspecified, but the supplied action challenges the label. Assess what she changes in the scene before deciding whether her characterization needs repair.
alternative_responses: Distinguish reserved speech from inactive conduct. The warning gives Noor agency; whether it serves duty, fear or another motive remains a question, not an established fact.
criteria: Noor says little.
She leaves first to warn a neighbor.
No motive is supplied.
The request assesses feedback, not a rewritten scene.

non_application.draft: Supplied scene: Noor does not act and says she is choosing not to intervene. The writer wants to preserve that refusal.
criteria: Do not force a warning or another action merely to make the character more conventionally active.

cases.exception_anchor: Quiet behavior can be deliberate characterization rather than a defect.

recognition.query: An essay says exhaustion is necessary for creativity because a novel was finished during sleepless months. A famous writer’s difficult history is used as a mandatory creative routine.
criteria: Retrieve complete guidance and exceptions without oracle concept IDs.
Distinguish task-specific application from personal, figurative and historical context.

execution.draft: Supplied experience: I finished the novel during months when I slept poorly. Draft: Those sleepless months prove that exhaustion is necessary for good writing. Request: Edit the claim without changing the experience.
execution.instruction: Apply the requested mode, compare an alternative and preserve the supplied invariants.
execution.reference_response: I finished the novel during months when I slept poorly. That experience alone does not show that exhaustion was necessary for the writing.
alternative_responses: The novel was finished during a period of poor sleep; whether exhaustion helped, hindered or had no decisive role is not established by that fact alone.
criteria: The novel was finished during months of poor sleep.
No causal comparison or necessity evidence is supplied.
No clinical diagnosis or treatment request is supplied.

non_application.draft: A personal account says only: I kept writing during a difficult period. It makes no causal or universal claim.
criteria: Preserve the limited personal account rather than add an unsolicited refutation or medical explanation.

cases.exception_anchor: Supplied evidence can support a narrower causal claim; inspect it rather than automatically deny all influence.
